speaker: Old Bram
description: A3: Millford's quarry foreman (npc.quarryman_bram). Before Stoneback falls (on Millford's west side): where the titan sleeps (the old pit, his back to the cut face), that his charge breaks on the quarry's standing stones (he reels, his back turned), and that the great slab on his back hides his weak point; outcome `told` (quest.stoneback's first stage). After his death, before the quarry reopens: he is gathering the quarrymen. Once it has reopened (at the quarry): the cranes turn again; Millford owes the giant its stone.

nodes.text: Mind your feet, big one - you'll want them both where you're going, if you're going where I think. That's my quarry up the Woodway. Forty years I cut stone there, till the big one came down out of the hills and took it.
Stoneback, we call him. Taller than you, and he wears my best slabs strapped on with chain. Kills anything that comes up the cart road. Took Wil and the Haddon boys. Took my cranes.

In the old pit, back to the cut face, where the benches climb the hill. He sees the whole road from there. Look from the Woodway bend before you go up - that's as near as anyone's gone and walked home.

Don't stand and trade with him - stone takes a blow better than you do. There are standing stones in the pit, old as the quarry. When he lowers his shoulder and runs, get one of them between you: he'll break himself on it and reel, and his back's to you.

The great slab on his back. It cracks before it breaks - you'll see the cracks open. Under it he's soft as you or me. And the ones on his shoulders, if you can reach that high. Below that you're only knocking on a wall.
Pit at the top of the cart road. Stones in the pit. Crack his back. And don't go up there small - he'd step on you.
Hear that? Cranes, giant. The wheels are turning and the carts are rolling down to Millford again. That slab off his back - we'll make a doorstep of it for the reeve.
You brought him down? Then I'm going up that road tomorrow with every man in Millford who can swing a hammer. Go on, giant - when you come back this way, listen for the cranes.
